s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and facial syndrome with mass effect
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum
Left upper eyelid mass previously excised on 3 separate occasions
Painless proptosis developed four months later
Left-sided facial numbness developed seventeen months later
Histopathology showed multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
MRI showed lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Genetic testing revealed a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and facial syndrome with mass effect
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum
Left upper eyelid mass previously excised on 3 separate occasions
Painless proptosis developed four months later
Left-sided facial numbness developed seventeen months later
Histopathology showed multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
MRI showed lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Genetic testing revealed a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a painless, left upper eyelid mass, proptosis, and left-sided facial numbness, along with histopathology showing a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, and immunohistochemistry positive for CD68, is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease. The disease is also known for its involvement of the orbits and central nervous system, which aligns with the patient's MRI findings.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with lymphadenopathy and is positive for S100, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with a different immunohistochemical profile, including positivity for CD1a and S100.

rejected.label: Histiocytic sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more aggressive clinical course and different histopathological features.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's history of Hodgkin lymphoma is noted, but the current presentation and histopathology are not consistent with a lymphoma recurrence.
